title: Should I Buy Assets Personally or Through My Corporation?

rows.before: Assets that earn business income belong in the corporation: bought with pre-tax dollars taxed near 12.2%, depreciated, HST recovered.
rows.after: Assets that earn business income belong in the corporation: bought with pre-tax dollars taxed near 11.2% (12.2% before July 1, 2026), depreciated, HST recovered.

rows.section: Investments: The Deferral and Its Two Prices
rows.before: money that would have shrunk past 53% on the way out instead compounds from a base taxed near 12.2%.
rows.after: money that would have shrunk past 53% on the way out instead compounds from a base taxed near 11.2%.

rows.section: FAQ - Why do people say corporate dollars are cheaper?
rows.before: Because the corporation keeps roughly 87.8 cents of each active dollar after the small business rate of about 12.2%, while a top-bracket owner keeps under 47 cents after personal tax above 53%.
rows.after: Because the corporation keeps roughly 88.8 cents of each active dollar after the small business rate of about 11.2%, while a top-bracket owner keeps under 47 cents after personal tax above 53%.
rows.note: R4: 87.8 cents = 100 - 12.2; at 11.2% it is 100 - 11.2 = 88.8 cents. Sharad to confirm figure.
